title: Validator-metric suite for measuring soundness, coverage, and operational impact of GVR oracles in NetOps
research_question: Can a standardized, empirically estimable validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact score) predict end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single raw verifier pass rate?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A multi-dimensional validator metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate (primary confirmatory hypothesis).
H2: Injected, preregistered realistic fault classes permit stable estimation of validator false-negative and false-positive rates under the controlled benchmark.
H3: Validator metrics correlate with a preregistered simulated operational-impact cost proxy and can be used to prioritize verifier development.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which injected fault classes (syntactic, semantic, configuration-logic, policy-violation) most strongly drive false-negative/false-positive tradeoffs?
EQ2: How sensitive are validator-metric estimates and predictive performance to alternative operational-cost parameterizations?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic paired NetOps GVR episodes generated via the supplied synthetic_paired_llm_benchmark_v1 / hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family.
Stress-test task-index profile: challenging_workflow_stress_v1 (adapter-prescribed 'very_hard' and 'extreme' generator levels).
secondary_estimands: per-validator false-positive rate (FP-rate) averaged across tasks
per-validator false-negative rate (FN-rate) averaged across tasks
R^2 of linear model predicting simulated operational-impact score from validator metric vectors
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design using hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter with task_count = 200 (required_confirmatory_task_count). Task selection follows the deterministic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index rule (indices fixed before any hosted-model call). Episodes: 2 per task (baseline, guarded) for 400 episodes total. Model-call budget: exactly task_count * 2 = 400. Because adapter does not guarantee deterministic sampling, one initial generation per task is preregistered as the shared initial candidate for the paired conditions; runtime sampling parameters (provider model name/version, temperature and other sampling parameters) will be recorded in the execution manifest for reproducibility and reported alongside results.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: detect an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 (10 percentage points) with alpha=0.05 (two-sided) and ~80% power. Recommended scenario: n=200 paired tasks (scenario_recommended_200). Calculation: approximate paired-proportion normal calculation under conservative baseline p=0.50 with sensitivity analyses for baseline p in {0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7} and within-pair correlations ρ in {0,0.1,0.2,0.3}. Bootstrap stability checks: 1,000 resamples to derive empirical SEs and CIs.
exclusion_rules: Exact-duplicate outputs (identical SHA-256) → automatic exclusion from confirmatory set and log as contamination-exclusion; replacement follows deterministic next-index rule to preserve task_count.
Near-duplicate tasks (embedding cosine similarity > 0.95) → deterministic exclusion and replacement by next-index to preserve task_count.
Repaired configurations that omit any preregistered mandatory parameters (deterministic rule) → automatic failure for that episode (counts as episode completed but unsuccessful).
Repairs that introduce actions outside the task's predeclared allowed action set → exclusion from primary success numerator and logging as policy-violation repair.
Validator-overfitting signal (>20 percentage-point FP/FN divergence between seeded and held-out generator set) → affected validator relegated to exploratory-only analyses.
missingness_plan: Adapter/infrastructure failures: maximum_attempts_per_call=1 (no manual retries). Primary analysis: complete-pair analysis only (paired_binary_analysis_v1 default). Sensitivity analysis: treat any missing/incomplete episode as failure (0) for the guarded condition (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity). All missingness metadata (timestamps, HTTP codes, provider error messages) logged in the execution manifest. No human adjudication or imputation will be used.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (compatible with the registered adapter). Primary test: paired two-condition difference in binary success (guarded vs baseline) using the executor's paired-proportion / permutation procedure; report point estimate, 95% CI, and p-value. Failed-call handling: primary analysis uses complete pairs only; sensitivity analysis treats incomplete pairs as failures (0) for guarded episodes. Secondary analyses: linear/robust regression predicting simulated operational-impact score from validator metric vectors; report adjusted R^2 and AUC for binary impact-thresholded outcomes. Bootstrap (1,000 resamples) for stability of metric estimates and predictive statistics. Report all analysis code, executor configuration, and runtime sampling parameters in published artifacts.
multiplicity_plan: Single pre-registered primary estimand (paired success-rate difference). All subgroup, per-error-class, per-validator, and cost-parameter analyses are exploratory. When reporting multiple p-values for exploratory hypothesis tests, control false discovery rate (Benjamini–Hochberg). Otherwise report effect sizes and confidence intervals without formal multiplicity claims.
contamination_plan: Detect and remove contamination via deterministic duplicate-detection (SHA-256) and semantic-similarity screening (embedding cosine > 0.95) with deterministic exclusions and deterministic replacement indices. Run validators against a held-out generator set to detect overfitting; if validator FP/FN diverges >20 percentage points compared to seeded set, relegate that validator to exploratory analyses. All exclusions, replacements, and contamination logs are published with raw artifacts. Confirmatory analyses use contamination-cleaned data; sensitivity analyses report results including flagged items.
stopping_rule: Stop when all preregistered task_indices (per deterministic index rule) have been processed or when maximum_model_calls = task_count * 2 = 400 is reached. No post-hoc sample changes; any early termination due to infrastructure failure is logged and reported as a technical failure (separate from scientific failure).
planned_outputs: Preregistered machine-readable experiment plan and execution manifest
Execution artifacts: raw model outputs, validator traces, hashes, and logs
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix
IEEE-format LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) and compiled PDF including mandatory Disclosure Statement
